tagline: A Pueblo road connects the Rio Grande with volcanic cliff dwellings.
intro: Puye Cliffs Scenic Byway follows Indian Road 565 for 14 miles on Santa Clara Pueblo land. The Federal Highway Administration allows an hour for the drive and presents its cultural and historic places as the route’s draw. It is New Mexico’s only state scenic byway entirely on an Indian Pueblo.
The route reaches dwellings carved into volcanic rock and expanded with adobe buildings on the slopes and mesa tops. In 2000, the Cerro Grande Fire devastated Santa Clara Canyon.

Begin with Santa Clara Pueblo on the Rio Grande, where potters make polished black and red pottery with incised designs. The journey continues across the reservation to Puye Cliff Dwellings in Santa Clara Canyon, with two levels of cliff rooms and a village on the mesa above.

moments.title: Santa Clara Pueblo
moments.text: Santa Clara Pueblo’s pottery includes polished black and red wares, with designs cut into the surface. Knife-wing and eagle feather designs are common, alongside painted designs, impressed patterns and resist-firing with incised or sgraffito decoration. Women and girls traditionally made most of the pottery; men also practice the craft now. This is a Tewa community on the Rio Grande, between Ohkay Owingeh to the north and San Ildefonso Pueblo to the south, whose people speak Rio Grande Tewa. The pueblo belongs to the Eight Northern Pueblos and is a federally recognized tribe of Tewa Pueblo people.

moments.title: Santa Clara Pueblo Land
moments.text: The byway lies entirely on an Indian Pueblo, but the reservation extends beyond the village that gives it its name. Santa Clara Pueblo land reaches into Rio Arriba, Sandoval and Santa Fe counties. Española is the largest community on reservation land, although part of the city lies outside the reservation. Much of Española also falls within the byway’s visual corridor.

moments.title: Puye Cliff Dwellings
moments.text: Puye’s rooms were carved from volcanic tuff soft enough to excavate with wooden tools. Two levels of cliff dwellings accompany surface and cave dwellings; a multistory village occupied the mesa top. A large plaza stood at the center of the complex. In 1907, Edgar Hewett excavated Puye with the Southwest Society of the Archaeological Institute of America. The ruins became a National Historic Landmark in 1966. The Community House is a reconstruction, part of a complex linked by paths, stairways and ladders. One level of cliff dwellings extends for more than a mile; the second runs about 2,100 feet along the rock.
moments.notice: Two levels of cliff dwellings occupy the volcanic rock below the mesa-top village.
